summary: On damaged storage (the owner's board: Directory corrupted) every ride is silently lost: journal appends, summary append and rename are refused, app_ride_save() returns false but the Results SAVE button ignores it (no toast), ride id still advances. Violates brief s5 'never silently discard unsynchronised rides'.
evidence (file:line): firmware/waveshare/main/ui/ui_results.c:17; main/app/app.c:305-316 (app_ride_save), :126-131 (jflush); main/plat_esp.c:73,94-97 (fs_may_write refuses); test/sim/sim_main.c:1900-1903 asserts the refusal, no warning
repro / how verified: sim section 24d: storage DIR_CORRUPTED, app_ride_start/end/save -> no file, no on-screen message; serial only 'RIDE SAVED #n FAILED'. TEST-v0.7.4 D4 will hit this on the owner's board.

summary: Automatic nvs_flash_erase() remains: on ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES or NEW_VERSION_FOUND the whole NVS (settings, sensor pairings, phone bonds, ride-id counter, boot skip mask, the new boot-record ring) is erased without approval.
repro / how verified: Code reading. Owner NVS census (coord/evidence/flash-v073-backup/nvs.bin, counts only): 1 EMPTY page, 505 erased/reclaimable entries -> trigger unlikely during the physical test, but the path contradicts 'no erase without approval'.

summary: Recovery is not minimal: storage mount + root scan, app_diag_init (crash report build, FAT write, core-dump copy) and the NVS boot record all run BEFORE the recovery decision. A deterministic crash there (marker STORAGE, not skippable) also crashes RECOVERY -> endless loop, never a stable screen.
repro / how verified: qa-fw/probes/boot_probe.c S7: crash in storage stage, 12 boots -> 12 crash resets, 9 'RECOVERY' boots, 0 stable.

summary: NVS boot record never gets the crash PC/task when the FAT is healthy: app_diag_init copies the core dump to the FAT and erases the partition before diag_esp_bootrec_begin reads it. The FAT-independent record only has the PC when the FAT is broken.
repro / how verified: Code order. Healthy FAT + crash -> report + core-*.elf on FAT, bootrec crash_pc = 0.

summary: Core-dump partition is erased after the FAT copy without reading the copy back / comparing a CRC (brief s6: verification before deleting).
repro / how verified: Code reading: copied = per-chunk fwrite result only.

summary: Boot-record ring keeps only 4 boots and SKIPPED/OK boots overwrite the failing ones. On the owner's board the installer's own two boots fail -> BT disabled from boot 3; TEST A1+A2 add 4 boots before B2, so the per-step heap records are gone from the board when B2 asks for them (only the serial first-boot log keeps them).
repro / how verified: Ring model: boots 1-2 FAIL, 3-6 SKIPPED -> ring = 3..6, all 'Bluetooth off (disabled)'.

summary: On the boot where the '2 failed starts' rule disables Bluetooth, the Phone screen offers WHY? instead of RETRY (app_diag keeps a copy of the plan taken before the rule ran). RETRY appears only from the next boot.
repro / how verified: Sim probe (copy, section 25 with 3 boots instead of 12): FAIL sim_main.c:1950 'NO BLUETOOTH + RETRY' (log qa-fw/logs/sim_probe_retry.log).

summary: ring_save() ignores NVS write errors; with a stale ring holding 2 failures and NVS writes failing, Bluetooth is disabled on every boot and RETRY cannot re-enable it.
repro / how verified: boot_probe S8: BT disabled 1; after RETRY + restart disabled again 1, 0 attempts.

summary: Crash streak lives only in RTC memory and is cleared 20 s after start: a crash later than 20 s after every start loops forever without RECOVERY; if RTC were lost at a crash reset, a BT-start panic would loop forever (no NVS-backed limiter). Real 0.7.3 log shows the RTC streak does survive panics (1,2,3).
repro / how verified: boot_probe S6: 12/12 crash resets, 0 RECOVERY; S4 (RTC lost): 12 crash resets, BT never disabled.

summary: A hang (not a crash) inside the controller/NimBLE start is not caught: task WDT does not panic (CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_PANIC unset), main task not subscribed, UI not started yet -> blank screen with no recovery.
repro / how verified: Code/config reading; only the board can show whether this happens.

summary: Hook registered for the whole run and for every task: during the BT stage the LVGL/esp_timer tasks already run, so 'first failed allocation' can belong to another task; the callback is in flash while IDF calls it from IRAM heap code (cache-disabled/ISR contexts would fault). Plain non-atomic stores (benign).
repro / how verified: Code reading vs /opt/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.1/components/heap/heap_caps.c:49-53.

summary: Corruption heuristic only catches total loss: a root with any free slot, or < 50 % erased/garbage entries, is probed and then written normally (writes into a damaged directory); a root full of valid + garbage entries is reported as 'Storage full'.
repro / how verified: Synthetic facts: 512 entries, 128 erased (one WL sector), 384 free -> corrupt_root false -> mkdir/probe write -> OK.

summary: Backup is read with esptool's default --after hard-reset, so the crash-looping 0.7.3 runs (and, per the FW report, touches the damaged FAT) between the verified backup and the write; the first rc1 boot after write-flash is not recorded (port opened after esptool's reset, then a second RTS reset); the result check ignores BOOTREC lines.
repro / how verified: Code reading; evidence install-v073 log shows 'Hard resetting via RTS pin' between backup and write.
